title: What to eat
intro: All but one of these are walk-in with no advance booking, ever. Mousel's Cantine gets busy at dinner, so a same-day call helps if arriving in the evening — Kaito Ramen and Manzoku Ramen Bar below are genuine no-reservation fallbacks if that doesn't pan out.

items.name: Marché Place Guillaume II
items.how: In the main square, a 5-minute walk from the Palace and Cathedral.
items.why: Regional produce, cheese, roast chicken and a food-stall cluster — the easiest, most casual lunch in the old town, and it lands on this trip's Saturday.

items.name: Mousel's Cantine
items.area: Clausen, at the foot of the Bock
items.how: A 10-minute walk downhill from Bock Casemates — a natural stop after the tunnels.
items.crowd_tip: Lunch generally seats walk-ins; dinner fills up, especially Fri–Sat — call ahead or use the online booking form if arriving after 19:00.
items.why: 200 years in the same Clausen building, serving Judd mat Gaardebounen — smoked pork collar and broad beans, Luxembourg's national dish.

items.name: Oberweis
items.hours: ⚠ Tearoom ≈Mon–Sat 08:00–17:15, shop ≈07:45–18:00, closed Sundays — confirm against the shop before relying on it
items.how: On the main shopping street, a few minutes from the Palace and Cathedral.
items.why: Family-run since 1964 and supplier to the Grand Ducal court since 1999 — a coffee-and-pastry break between old-town sights, not a full meal.

items.name: Kaito Ramen
items.area: Place de Paris, near the central train station
items.how: Walk-in / first-come-first-served every day of this trip's stay; only groups of 8+ can book ahead.
items.crowd_tip: Gets genuinely busy at midday — arriving by or around noon, or going for dinner instead, is the practical way to skip the wait.
items.why: Open every day of the Oct 16–19 stay with zero reservation system for parties this size — the most reliable no-booking dinner or lunch fallback on this list.

items.name: Manzoku Ramen Bar
items.area: ⚠ Exact street address not independently confirmed this pass — check manzoku.lu before going
items.how: No reservation system exists at all — once full, seating runs off a virtual waitlist app.
items.why: Genuinely walk-in-only by design, matching a no-formal-booking preference exactly — but only Friday and Saturday of this Fri–Mon stay fall inside its open days.
